item.title: Can Bruno Fernandes really break the Premier League’s weirdest record?

item.description: Due to differences between the countries’ voting systems, Britain may have more far-right councils in May than its neighbour, writes long-term French elections observer Mary Dejevsky

item.description: Guardiola outsmarted his ‘apprentice’ Arteta at Wembley as Man City won the Carabao Cup to lay down a psychological marker in the battle for Premier League glory

item.title: For their sake, Sudan’s displaced children can’t wait for diplomacy
item.description: Five million children have been displaced by Sudan’s war. As the UK prepares to co-host a global conference on the third anniversary of the Sudan war, Moazzam Malik, CEO of Save the Children UK, urges the world to pay more attention

item.title: AI, a dead student, and US airstrikes: The civilian caught up in a new age of warfare
item.description: As debate grows over the role of AI in military strikes in the bombing of Iran, scrutiny has turned to civilians caught up in the destruction. An investigation by The Independent and conflict monitoring group Airwars explores the death of a 20-year-old killed in a US strike in Iraq in 2024 – the first known victim of an airstrike in which the use of AI-assisted targeting was acknowledged. Namir Shabibi and Alex Croft report

item.title: Is North Sea oil and gas set to be Keir Starmer’s next U-turn?

item.title: Is it time to stock up? The hidden soaring cost about to affect your supermarket shop
item.description: War in the Middle East is pushing up the cost of fuel, fertiliser and freight and it could affect everything from bread, pasta and cereals. Hannah Twiggs explains what that means for the price of your weekly shop and whether stocking up now makes sense
